just · already · yet — Grammar Easy

12 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat. All the examples are about Lucy's to-do list.Прочитайте четыре шага. Нажмите 🔊 и повторите. Все примеры — о списке дел Люси.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаjust · already · yet
1
Одна мысль

Present perfect (have / has + V3) — это новость или результат сейчас: чемодан собран, страховка куплена. Три маленьких слова: just = только что, already = уже (раньше, чем думали), yet = уже? (в вопросе) / ещё не (с not). just и already стоят между have и V3, yet — в самом конце.

2
Формула-конструктор
I've+just+got+the email.
She's+already+packed+her suitcase.

just / already → между have и V3

I haven't+bought+insurance+yet.
Have you+checked in+yet?

yet → в конце, только в вопросе и с not. Короткий ответ: No, not yet.

3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • I've just got the email.
  • She's already packed her suitcase.
  • I haven't bought travel insurance yet.
  • Have you checked in yet?
  • Has she set an alarm? — No, not yet.
4
Осторожно!
❌ I've packed my suitcase yet. → ✅ I've already packed my suitcase.
yet — только в вопросе и с not
❌ I've checked already in. → ✅ I've already checked in.
already — между have и V3
❌ She have just arrived. → ✅ She has just arrived.
he / she → has

b Step 1. Meaning. Which word is it?Шаг 1. Какое это слово?

  1. только что →
  2. уже (раньше, чем думали) →
  3. ещё не… (с not, в конце) →
  4. уже? (в вопросе, в конце) →

  1. I haven't changed any money .

  5. The taxi has arrived. It's outside the door now!
  6. Sam, I've bought the tickets. I did it last week.

d Step 3. Build. just / already in the middle, yet at the end.Шаг 3. Соберите. just / already — в середине, yet — в конце.

  4. (she / check in) yet?
  5. Sam (already / call) her twice today.
  6. «I (not / say) goodbye to my cat yet!»

messages from the Red Sea

a Lucy is in Egypt now. She sends Sam messages from the dive centre. Read them. How does she feel about deep water now?Люси уже в Египте и пишет Сэму. Прочитайте. Как она теперь относится к глубине?

Lucy · Day 1

Hi Sam! I've just arrived at the hotel. The flight was fine — I slept all the way. It's so hot here! I'm glad I packed two bottles of sun cream.

Lucy · Day 2

I've already had two lessons in the swimming pool. Yesterday the instructor showed us how to breathe under water. It was strange, but I didn't panic! I haven't been in the sea yet — that's tomorrow.

Lucy · Day 3

I did it!!! At ten o'clock this morning we went down twelve metres. I saw a turtle and hundreds of fish. I've never seen anything so beautiful. And guess what? I'm not afraid of deep water any more!

Lucy · Day 5

Last night I tried a very strange fish dish — another «yes»! And I've just booked another diving course for next year. Have you booked your summer holiday yet? Come with me!

How does Lucy feel about deep water now?

present perfect or past simple? — Grammar Easy

10 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat. The examples are from Lucy's call and her messages.Прочитайте четыре шага и повторите. Примеры — из звонка и сообщений Люси.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаpresent perfect or past simple?
1
Одна мысль

Сначала — новость, без времени: present perfect (I've just arrived!). Потом — детали: когда? где? как? — past simple (The flight was fine. I slept all the way.). Видите слово-время — yesterday, last week, at ten o'clock, in August, two days ago, When…? — значит, только past simple.

2
Формула-конструктор
I've+just+arrived+at the hotel.
The flight+landed+at six.

Без времени (just, already, yet, ever, never) → have / has + V3 · Есть время → V2 (past simple)

Have you+ever+been+diving?
When+did you+go?

Вопрос «Have you ever…?» → ответ «Yes, I have.» → детали: When did you…? Where did you…?

3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • I've just arrived at the hotel.
  • I slept all the way on the plane.
  • I saw a turtle at ten o'clock this morning.
  • I've never seen anything so beautiful.
  • I renewed my passport in August.
4
Осторожно!
❌ I've arrived yesterday. → ✅ I arrived yesterday.
yesterday → past simple
❌ When have you arrived? → ✅ When did you arrive?
When…? → past simple
❌ I've seen a turtle two days ago. → ✅ I saw a turtle two days ago.
ago → past simple

  3. When the diving course?

  5. Host: (you / book) your next trip yet?
  6. Lucy: Yes, I (already / book) a course for next year.
  7. Host: When (you / book) it?
  8. Lucy: Last night. And I (not / tell) my mum yet!

Max's dilemma

10 min

a Listen to the podcast «The Decision Desk». Max has a big decision to make — and it's a risky one. What is his dilemma?

Podcast: «The Decision Desk»Listen first · Use 🐢 if it's fast · Text at the end
  1. Clare (host):Hello and welcome to The Decision Desk, the podcast that helps you make the big decisions. Our first caller today is Max. Hi, Max. What's your dilemma?
  2. Max:Hi, Clare. So, I'm thirty-six, I'm an engineer, and I've worked for the same company for eleven years. It's a good, stable job, and I can afford to play it safe. But last month a friend offered me a job at his start-up in Lisbon.
  3. Clare (host):And you can't make up your mind.
  4. Max:Exactly. I keep changing my mind. One day I want to go for it, and the next day I have second thoughts. My wife is happy to move, but my parents are trying to talk me out of it. They say it's a gamble.
  5. Clare (host):What does your gut tell you?
  6. Max:Honestly? To accept. But I don't want to make a mistake. I tend to overthink everything.
  7. Clare (host):Have you tried writing down the pros and cons?
  8. Max:Yes, I've already weighed them up. The salary is lower, but I'd own five percent of the company. And I've ruled out asking for more money — they really can't afford it.
  9. Clare (host):OK, here's my advice. First, stop trying to find the perfect answer. It doesn't exist. Second, remember to sleep on it before you reply. And third, imagine you're eighty. Which would you regret more: going and failing, or not going at all?
  10. Max:Not going. Definitely.
  11. Clare (host):Then I think you already know the answer. And Max, once you decide, stick with your decision. Don't waste time second-guessing yourself.
  12. Max:Thanks, Clare. I'll let you know what happens.

Max can't decide whether to…

verb + -ing or to

13 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. The examples are from Max's call.

Grammar Bank2Agerunds and infinitives
patterncommon verbs and phrasesexample
verb + -ingavoid, consider, can't stand, enjoy, finish, imagine, keep, mind, miss, risk, suggest, give up, rule out, waste timeI keep changing my mind.
preposition + -inginstead of, before, after, without, by; good at, think about, look forward toInstead of playing it safe, she went for it.
-ing as the subjectChanging careers is a gamble.
verb + to + verbafford, agree, decide, expect, hope, manage, offer, plan, promise, refuse, seem, tend, want, would likeI can't afford to lose my salary.
adjective + to + verbhappy, ready, willing, easy, hardMy wife is happy to move.
verb + object + toadvise, ask, encourage, persuade, tell, want, would likeMy parents want me to stay.
make / let + object + verbThey let me work from home.
  • In look forward to the word to is a preposition, so: I'm looking forward to working with you.
  • Negatives: not goes before the verb: He decided not to ask. I regret not going.
  • suggest + -ing (or suggest that…), never suggest to do.

Five ways to stop overthinking

8 min

a After Max's call, Clare wrote an article for the podcast's website. Read it. Which tip would help you most?

Five ways to stop overthinking · by Clare, host of «The Decision Desk»

1. Stop trying to be perfect. There is rarely a perfect option, only a good-enough one. And if you stop to analyse every small choice, you'll be exhausted by lunchtime.

2. Try sleeping on it. Our brains go on working while we sleep, so the answer often seems clearer in the morning. Big decisions are tiring, so try to make them early in the day, not at midnight.

3. Remember your good decisions. Do you remember making a choice that really paid off? How did it feel? And remember to ask yourself the same question every time: "What would I tell a friend in my situation?"

4. Set a deadline — and don't forget to tell someone about it. Many of us never forget making one bad decision, and that memory makes us play it safe for years.

5. Think about regret. Research suggests that in the long term, people regret the things they didn't do more than the things they did. As one listener told us: "I regret not applying to art school. Nobody ever regrets trying."

Clare's main message is that…

Grammar Bank2Averbs that change their meaning
verb+ to + verb+ -ing
remembera task — first you remember, then you do it: Remember to ask yourself…a memory of the past: Do you remember making that choice?
forgetnot do a task: Don't forget to tell someone.(usually never forget) a memory: I'll never forget meeting her.
trymake an effort, it may be difficult: Try to make big decisions early in the day.do it as an experiment, to see if it helps: Try sleeping on it.
stoppause in order to do something: If you stop to analyse every choice…no longer do something: Stop trying to be perfect.
regretformal: be sorry to give bad news: We regret to inform you that…be sorry about the past: I regret not applying.
go ondo the next thing: He worked in a bank and then went on to start a company.continue: Our brains go on working while we sleep.

a ransomware attack in the news

a Listen to a radio news report about Brightwell, an online furniture retailer. You will hear most of the new words. What happened to the company?

Radio: «Tech Brief»Listen first · Use 🐢 if it's fast · Text at the end
  1. Hannah (presenter):Good evening and welcome to Tech Brief. Our top story tonight: the online furniture retailer Brightwell has been hit by a ransomware attack. Its website was taken offline on Saturday morning, and it still hasn't been restored. With me is security analyst Owen Price. Owen, what do we know so far?
  2. Owen (security analyst):Well, the attack seems to have started late on Friday night. Thousands of files were encrypted, including the systems that handle orders and deliveries. On Saturday morning, staff arrived to find a ransom note on every screen.
  3. Hannah (presenter):How much are the attackers asking for?
  4. Owen (security analyst):The ransom is said to be around four million dollars. Brightwell hasn't confirmed that, but the company says it won't pay.
  5. Hannah (presenter):And how did the attackers get in?
  6. Owen (security analyst):That's still being investigated. But it's believed that an employee's account was compromised in a phishing attack. If that's right, the attackers must have used that account to log in to the company's network, and the login wasn't protected by two-factor authentication.
  7. Hannah (presenter):So could the attack have been prevented?
  8. Owen (security analyst):Probably, yes. The attackers used a vulnerability that had been known about for months. A patch was released in March, but it was never installed. That server should have been patched long ago.
  9. Hannah (presenter):What about customers? Has their data been stolen?
  10. Owen (security analyst):We don't know yet. Customers are being contacted by email today, and the breach will have to be disclosed to the regulator within seventy-two hours. The good news is that Brightwell's backups weren't affected, so the systems can be restored. But the downtime is expensive: it's costing the company an estimated half a million pounds a day.
  11. Hannah (presenter):Owen Price, thank you.

What happened to Brightwell?

the passive: all forms

13 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. The examples are from the Brightwell story. Notice that the passive is always be (in the right form) + past participle.

Grammar Bank2Athe passive — all forms
formactivepassive
present simpleWe patch the servers every month.The servers are patched every month.
present continuousA team is investigating the attack.The attack is being investigated.
past simpleThe ransomware encrypted thousands of files.Thousands of files were encrypted.
past continuousThey were copying the data at 2 a.m.The data was being copied at 2 a.m.
present perfectSomeone has stolen customer data.Customer data has been stolen.
past perfectExperts had known about the vulnerability.The vulnerability had been known about.
future · modalWe will / can restore the systems.The systems will / can be restored.
modal + have (past)They should have patched the server.The server should have been patched.
  • We use the passive when the action or the result is more important than who did it, when we don't know who did it, and in formal reports.
  • Add by + agent only when it is important: The attack is being investigated by the police.
  • Passive infinitive and -ing: All accounts need to be checked. Nobody likes being hacked.
  • Last lesson's modals work in the passive too: The password must have been stolen.

Подсказка. По-русски часто говорят без подлежащего: «Сервер взломали», «Данные уже восстанавливают». По-английски это пассив: The server was hacked. The data is being restored. Не забывайте be: ❌ The server hacked.

the post-incident report

a One week later Brightwell's security team writes a report for the board. Read it. What is its main message?

Post-incident report · Ransomware attack · Summary for the board

What happened. Late on Friday night, Brightwell was hit by a ransomware attack. Around forty thousand files were encrypted, and the website and the warehouse systems had to be taken offline. They were restored from backups after five days of downtime. No ransom was paid.

How the attackers got in. The investigation has not been completed, but the attackers are believed to have entered the network through an old VPN server. The login details of a sales manager are thought to have been stolen in a phishing attack two weeks earlier. The server was not protected by two-factor authentication, and a known vulnerability had not been patched.

Root cause. It is now clear that the root cause was organisational, not technical: nobody was responsible for the old server. It had been forgotten when the company moved its systems to the cloud last year.

Customer data. It is estimated that the personal data of about twelve thousand customers was copied. The breach was disclosed to the regulator within seventy-two hours, and all affected customers have been contacted.

Next steps. We are having the whole network audited by an external security firm, and all staff will be trained to recognise phishing. Two-factor authentication must be switched on for every account by the end of the month. Finally, we will have our backups tested every quarter.

Grammar Bank2Areporting passives · have something done
structureexampleuse

a Now listen to the podcast «Fresh Starts». Lucy interviews Olga. You will hear the words from the Vocabulary Bank. How does Olga feel about her new life now?Послушайте подкаст: Люси берёт интервью у Ольги. Вы услышите слова урока. Как Ольга чувствует себя сейчас?

Podcast: «Fresh Starts»Listen first · Если быстро — нажмите 🐢 · Текст — в конце
  1. Lucy (host):Hello and welcome to «Fresh Starts», the podcast about people who changed their lives. My guest today is Olga. She was an accountant in Kazan, and now she lives in a small village by the sea in Montenegro. Olga, how long have you lived here?
  2. Olga:I've lived here for about a year and a half. I moved here in March last year.
  3. Lucy (host):Why did you decide to move abroad?
  4. Olga:For twenty years I was stuck in a rut: home, office, home. So I took a year off and came here. It was the best decision of my life.
  5. Lucy (host):Was it easy at first?
  6. Olga:No, not at all! It was a real culture shock. Everything was different: the food, the language, even the time people have dinner. And I was terribly homesick. I missed my family and my friends.
  7. Lucy (host):And how do you feel now?
  8. Olga:Now I feel at home here. I've made a lot of friends, and the locals are very kind. My neighbour Milena is my best friend here. I've known her since my first day in the village.
  9. Lucy (host):Do you speak the language?
  10. Olga:A little! I've picked up a lot of words from Milena and her family. And I've studied with a teacher since January.
  11. Lucy (host):How do you earn a living?
  12. Olga:I paint! I took up painting when I arrived, and I've sold more than sixty pictures since then. Last month I opened a tiny gallery by the sea.
  13. Lucy (host):Do you keep in touch with your friends in Kazan?
  14. Olga:Of course. We have a video call every Sunday. My sister visited me in the summer, and she loved it here.
  15. Lucy (host):Are you going to go back?
  16. Olga:I don't think so. I went to Kazan last Christmas, but I haven't been back since then. Honestly, this life is a dream come true. I think I've finally settled down.

How does Olga feel about her new life now?

present perfect + for / since

a Read the Grammar Bank. All the examples are like Olga's sentences from the podcast. Look at the colours: the formula has two parts.Прочитайте Grammar Bank. Все примеры — как фразы Ольги из подкаста. Формула из двух частей.

Grammar Bank2Apresent perfect + for / since: How long?
have / has + V3I've lived hereI've known · she's had · we've been · I haven't seen
+
for + a period · since + a pointfor two years · since 2024for a week · for ages · since March · since I was a child

It started in the past and it is still true now. The question: How long have you…?

for + a period (сколько времени)since + a point (с какого момента)
for two days · for a week · for six monthssince Monday · since March · since 2025
for a year and a half · for a long time · for agessince my first day · since then · since I was a child
❌ I live here for two years.
❌ I know her since my first day.
❌ How long do you live here?
❌ I've lived here since two years.
✅ I've lived here for two years.
✅ I've known her since my first day.
✅ How long have you lived here?
✅ I've lived here for two years.

Подсказка. По-русски мы говорим в настоящем времени: «Я живу здесь два года», «Я знаю её с первого дня». В английском, если действие началось в прошлом и продолжается до сих пор, нужен present perfect: I've lived, I've known. «… лет / месяцев / дней» → for. «с …» → since.

My name is Olga. I was born in Kazan, and I lived there for forty-four years. I worked as an accountant in a big company for twenty years. It wasn't a bad job, but I was stuck in a rut.

present perfect or past simple?

10 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. The examples are from Olga's website. One question helps every time: is it still true now?Прочитайте Grammar Bank. Помогает один вопрос: это правда и сейчас?

Grammar Bank2Apresent perfect or past simple?
past simple · When?I moved here in 2025.in March · last year · two years ago · when I arrived · finished: for 20 years
≠
present perfect · How long?I've lived here since 2025.for a year and a half · since then · still true now

Ask yourself: Is it still true now? Yes → present perfect. No, it's finished → past simple.

❌ I've moved here in 2025.
❌ When have you moved here?
❌ She's worked as an accountant for twenty years. (she doesn't now)
✅ I moved here in 2025. (in 2025, ago, last… → past simple)
✅ When did you move here?
✅ She worked as an accountant for twenty years. (finished)

Подсказка. «Я работала бухгалтером 20 лет» — сейчас уже нет → past simple: I worked. «Я живу здесь с 2025 года» — и сейчас тоже → present perfect: I've lived. Слова-подсказки: When? ago, last…, in 2025 → past simple. How long? since → present perfect. А for бывает в обоих — смотрите, закончилось или нет.

I like · Do you like…?

10 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat.Прочитайте четыре шага. Нажмите 🔊 и повторите.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаI like · I don't like · Do you like…?
1
Одна мысль

Нравится — I like pizza. Очень нравится — I love ice cream! Не нравится — I don't like salad. Спросить: Do you like cake? Ответ: Yes, I do. или No, I don't. Так же с we, you, they: We like… They don't like…

2
Формула-конструктор
I+like+pizza.
I+don't like+salad.
Do+you+like+cake?

😍 I love… · 🙂 I like… · 🙁 I don't like…

Ответ: Yes, I do. / No, I don't. — не «Yes, I like» и не «Yes, I can»!

3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • I love pizza!
  • I like chocolate.
  • I don't like salad.
  • Do you like cake? Yes, I do.
  • Do you like milk? No, I don't.
4
Осторожно!
❌ I not like salad. → ✅ I don't like salad.
«не» — don't
❌ You like pizza? → ✅ Do you like pizza?
вопрос — Do в начале
❌ Do you like cake? Yes, I like. → ✅ Yes, I do.
короткий ответ: Yes, I do.

Maya's camp blog

12 min

a Meet Maya. She is twelve, like you, and she is spending a week at a survival camp on a tiny Scottish island. Read her blog. Find six words from the Vocabulary Bank — and three words from our last lesson about animals!

Maya's blog · «Seven days in the wild»a blog · about 350 words

Day 1 · Hello, Kerra!
Hi everyone! I'm Maya, I'm twelve, and I'm spending a week at Wild Kids Camp on the Isle of Kerra, a tiny island off the west coast of Scotland. There are no shops, no cars and no Wi-Fi — just sixteen kids, four leaders and the wild! The island is the habitat of more than a hundred species of birds, and on the first evening we watched hundreds of puffins. They migrate here every spring. My bag was too heavy to carry up the hill — Mum packed too many clothes! And there are too many midges: tiny flying insects that bite. They love me.

Day 2 · The tent disaster
Today we put up our tents. It sounds easy, but it was too windy to do it quickly, and our tent was too small for four people, so my friend Zoe and I moved to another one. At night it was freezing. My sleeping bag wasn't warm enough, so I slept in my jumper, my hat and two pairs of socks!

Day 3 · Fire!
We learned to light a fire without matches. It took me forty minutes! The problem was the firewood: it wasn't dry enough, because it rained all morning. We were all soaked — my 'waterproof' jacket isn't waterproof at all. On the beach our leader showed us some birds' eggs. They have perfect camouflage: they look just like stones! In the evening we cooked fish over the fire. It was delicious, but there wasn't enough fish for everyone, so the leaders gave us extra bread.

Day 4 · Lost in the fog
Today we did a navigation challenge with a map and a compass. My team got lost in the fog for an hour — we were walking too fast to notice the path! But we found our way back. Tomorrow we're building shelters, and we can sleep in them if they're strong enough. I'm not sure I'm brave enough!

Look: warm enough, dry enough, but enough fish. Where does enough go?

too and enough

10 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. All the examples are from Maya's blog. Then do the exercises — the second one is an exam-style transformation.

Grammar Bank2Atoo · too much / too many · (not) enough
formmeaningexamples from the blog
too + adjectivemore than is OK — a problemOur tent was too small for four people.
too much + uncountable nounmore than you wantMum packed too much food.
too many + plural nounThere are too many midges. Mum packed too many clothes.
adjective + enoughas much as you needMy sleeping bag wasn't warm enough.
(not) enough + noun(not) as much / many as you needThere wasn't enough fish for everyone.
… + to + verb / for + personwhat is (not) possible / for whomtoo heavy to carry · too fast to notice · too small for four people
  • very ≠ too: The sea was very cold (but maybe we swam). The sea was too cold to swim in (we didn't!).
  • ❌ enough warm → ✅ warm enough · ❌ fish enough → ✅ enough fish · ❌ too much small → ✅ too small
  • Same meaning, two ways: The tent was too small. = The tent wasn't big enough.

Подсказка. too = «слишком» (это проблема!), enough = «достаточно». enough ставим ПОСЛЕ прилагательного (warm enough), но ПЕРЕД существительным (enough fish).

  1. The sea was cold to swim in.
  2. We didn't have firewood, so we collected more.
  3. There were midges — I had forty bites!
  4. Mum put food in my bag. It was so heavy!
  5. Are you old to go to a camp without your parents?
  6. This jacket isn't for a Scottish summer.

b Exam-style task. Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use one or two words.

  1. The tent was too small for four people.
    The tent wasn't for four people.
  2. The firewood was too wet to burn.
    The firewood wasn't to burn.
  3. Maya isn't old enough to go camping alone.
    Maya is to go camping alone.
  4. The water was too cold for swimming.
    The water wasn't for swimming.
  5. We had too little food.
    We didn't have food.
  6. It was too dark to see the path.
    It wasn't to see the path.

c Build the sentences.

Day 5: Maya calls home

9 min

a Maya wasn't sure she was brave enough to sleep in a shelter — remember? On Day 5 the campers can make one phone call home. Listen to Maya and her dad. Where did Maya sleep last night?

Phone call: Maya and her dadListen first · Use 🐢 if it's fast · Text at the end
  1. Dad:Maya! How are you, sweetheart? How's the island?
  2. Maya:Hi, Dad! It's amazing. I'm a bit tired, but I'm fine. Guess what — last night I slept in a shelter that I built myself!
  3. Dad:Wow! Was it warm enough?
  4. Maya:Not really — it was freezing! But it was strong enough, and it didn't fall down. A few people went back to their tents in the middle of the night, but I stayed.
  5. Dad:Well done! And are you eating enough?
  6. Maya:Yes, we've got plenty of food! Lots of fish and potatoes. But we've got hardly any chocolate left. I've only got a little hot chocolate powder and a few biscuits.
  7. Dad:Ha! And what about your pocket money? Have you spent much?
  8. Maya:Dad, there are no shops here! I haven't spent any money at all.
  9. Dad:Of course. And how are the midges?
  10. Maya:Terrible! There are too many of them, and I've got lots of bites. I need some more midge spray. Did you pack any?
  11. Dad:Yes, I did. It's in the small pocket of your bag.
  12. Maya:Oh, I didn't see it! Thanks, Dad.
  13. Dad:So what's the plan for tomorrow?
  14. Maya:Tomorrow is the big hike to the lighthouse. It's fourteen kilometres! We need plenty of water, and we can only take a little food, because our bags can't be too heavy.
  15. Dad:Have you got enough warm clothes?
  16. Maya:Yes — too many! You packed six jumpers, Dad! None of my friends have got more than two.
  17. Dad:OK, OK! Have a great hike, and call us on Sunday.
  18. Maya:I will. Love you! Bye!

a few, a little, plenty of, hardly any, none

a Read the Grammar Bank. The examples are from Maya's phone call. Countable or uncountable? Look at the noun first!

Grammar Bank2Aquantifiers
things you can count
biscuits, people, midges		things you can't count
food, water, chocolate
a large amountlots of / a lot of biscuitslots of / a lot of food
more than enough 😊plenty of torchesplenty of water
a small amounta few biscuitsa little chocolate
almost nothinghardly any midgeshardly any chocolate

questionsHow many jumpers?How much water?
  • no + noun: There are no shops. none — without a noun: How many shops are there? — None. or None of my friends…
  • hardly any already means «almost none», so the verb is positive: ❌ We haven't got hardly any → ✅ We've got hardly any chocolate.
  • In questions and negatives we often use much / many: Have you spent much? There aren't many midges today.
  • Challenge: a few = some (good!), few = not many (a pity): I've got a few friends here 😊 · Few people visit the island.

Подсказка. a few / a little = «немного, несколько»; plenty of = «полно, более чем достаточно»; hardly any = «почти нет»; none = «ни одного, нисколько» (без существительного). С исчисляемыми — few, many; с неисчисляемыми — little, much.

Emma's blog: the Oxford trip

a Now read Emma's new blog post. Find six phrases from the Vocabulary Bank. Was it a good day in the end?Найдите в блоге шесть фраз урока. Хорошим ли был день?

Emma's blog · «Oxford: a day to remember»

Last Saturday was my day off, and I went to Oxford with my sister, Lucy. I booked the train tickets a week before, and I was really looking forward to the trip.

But we were running late. At ten o'clock, when our train left, we were still buying coffee at the station! So we missed the train and caught the next one. We arrived in Oxford at half past eleven.

Jack was right: it was pouring with rain. People were hurrying along the streets, and tourists were hiding in cafés. I had my umbrella, but Lucy didn't, so she got soaked in five minutes. We went sightseeing anyway: we visited two old colleges and a museum.

At three o'clock we were sitting in a little café by the river and drinking hot chocolate. Suddenly the sun came out, and the city looked beautiful. We walked by the river and took lots of photos. We got back home at nine, tired but happy. In the end, the day turned out really well!

Oh, and I bumped into someone I didn't expect to see… but more about that later!

How was Emma's day in the end?

past simple vs past continuous

15 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. All the examples are from Emma's blog.

Grammar Bank2Bpast simple vs past continuous
past simplepast continuous
usefinished actions: what happened, one thing after anotheran action in progress at a time in the past · the background of a story
+We missed the train. Lucy got soaked.It was pouring with rain. We were buying coffee.
–Lucy didn't have an umbrella.We weren't walking — we were sitting in a café.
?What time did you get back?What were you doing at three o'clock?
form-ed or the irregular form: booked, went, got, tookwas / were + verb-ing
  • I / he / she / it → was …ing · you / we / they → were …ing.
  • Time phrases like at three o'clock, at that moment often go with the past continuous: At three o'clock we were sitting in a café.
  • State verbs (know, like, want, need, have = own) are not used in the continuous: ✗ I was having an umbrella ✓ I had an umbrella.

Подсказка. Past simple — «что произошло» (опоздали, промокла, вернулись). Past continuous — «что происходило» в тот момент, фон истории: «лил дождь, люди спешили». Повторявшиеся действия в прошлом — не continuous: I went there every summer.

  1. At ten o'clock Emma and Lucy coffee at the station.
  2. They the ten o'clock train by one minute.
  3. Lucy an umbrella, so she got soaked.
  4. What at three o'clock? — We were sitting in a café.
  5. They two old colleges and a museum.
  6. They back home at nine.

when and while

13 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. The examples are from Emma's story at Jack's.

Grammar Bank2Bwhen and while
the long action (past continuous)the short action (past simple)
whenShe was waiting for a buswhen she saw us.
whileWhile I was taking a photo,my phone ran out of battery.
  • while + the long action (was / were …ing). when usually + the short action (past simple).
  • When the sentence starts with When / While, put a comma in the middle: While I was taking a photo, my phone…
  • Two short actions, one after the other → past simple + past simple: When the sun came out, we walked by the river. (first the sun, then the walk)
  • Two long actions at the same time → while + past continuous: While Emma was talking, Jack was eating the cake.

Подсказка. Длинное действие (что происходило) — was / were + -ing; короткое, которое «врезалось» в него, — past simple. while ≈ «пока», when ≈ «когда (вдруг)».

  1. While we were walking to the first college, I into Anna.

  3. While I was taking a photo, my phone out of battery.
  4. We back to the station when we got lost.
  5. When the sun came out, we by the river.
  6. What when you bumped into Anna?

Anya's plan

8 min

a Read Anya's blog. Who is Helen? Find five words from the Vocabulary Bank.Прочитайте блог Ани. Кто такая Хелен? Найдите пять слов из Vocabulary Bank.

Anya's blog · «The woman who changed my life»

Five years ago I was living in London. One rainy morning I was going to an important job interview, but I couldn't find a taxi. Then a woman stopped her car and drove me to the interview. Later I saw her again — she was the director! Her name is Helen, and I got the job.

Now Helen is going to retire. Her last day at work is Friday the 28th, and I'm going to organise a surprise leaving party for her. We aren't going to tell her about it — everybody in the office is going to keep the secret!

Here's the plan. We're going to invite all her colleagues, old and new — about forty guests. Tom is going to find a band, and I'm going to make a short speech. We aren't going to buy flowers — Helen doesn't like them. We're going to give her a photo book with pictures from her twenty years at the company.

Helen loves surprises, so I think she's going to be very happy. And I'm sure she's going to cry! Am I nervous? Yes, I am. Is it going to be the best party ever? I hope so!

Who is Helen?

a Read the Grammar Bank. All the examples are from Anya's blog. Then do the exercise.Прочитайте Grammar Bank: все примеры — из блога Ани.

Grammar Bank2Abe going to
be going to + verb
+I'm going to organise a party. She's going to retire. We're going to invite forty guests.
−I'm not going to tell her. He isn't going to come. We aren't going to buy flowers.
?Are you going to make a speech? — Yes, I am. / No, I'm not. · What is Tom going to do?
useexample
a plan — you have decidedI'm going to organise a surprise party.
a prediction — you can see or you know something nowHelen loves surprises, so she's going to be very happy. · Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.
  • With go: I'm going to the party sounds more natural than I'm going to go to the party.
  • In fast speech going to often sounds like /ˈɡənə/ — but we write going to.

Подсказка. be going to = «собираюсь» (план, решение уже принято) или «уже видно, что…» (прогноз): «Смотри, какие тучи — сейчас пойдёт дождь». После going to — глагол в начальной форме: going to make, не going to makes и не going to making.

  1. Anya organise the party.
  2. We tell Helen. It's a secret!
  3. Tom going to find a band?
  4. What you going to buy her?
  5. I'm going a short speech.
  6. Look at those clouds! It rain.

present continuous for arrangements

10 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. The examples are from the phone call. Then decide: now or the future?Прочитайте Grammar Bank. Примеры — из телефонного разговора. Потом решите: сейчас или будущее?

Grammar Bank2Apresent continuous for future arrangements
formwhen?example
present continuous + a future timean arrangement: the day, time or place is fixed, other people know, you have bookedWe're meeting at the restaurant on Friday at seven. The band is playing from eight.
be going toa plan (decided, maybe no fixed time) · a predictionI'm going to make a speech. You're going to be great!
  • Use a future time word (tomorrow, on Friday, next week) — without it, I'm meeting Kate usually means now.
  • For arrangements both forms are often possible: I'm meeting Kate on Wednesday = I'm going to meet Kate on Wednesday. The present continuous sounds more fixed — it's in your diary.
  • Questions about plans: What are you doing on Saturday? Are you doing anything tonight?

Подсказка. По-русски мы тоже говорим о будущем в настоящем времени: «В пятницу мы встречаемся в семь». Есть договорённость (время, место, билеты) → present continuous. Прогноз — только going to: It's going to rain tomorrow.

From Lab to Headline

How does a modest study become a viral miracle? Dr Hart tells the story of her own research, a C1 article asks who is to blame for science hype — and you learn to say exactly what the evidence shows with distancing and hedging.

“Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence.”Carl Sagan

how my study went viral

10 min

a Dr Hart is back on «Mind Matters» — this time with a story about her own research. Listen. What, according to her, was the main problem?

Podcast: «Mind Matters»Listen first · Text at the end
  1. Host:Dr Hart, welcome back to «Mind Matters». Last time you told us that nobody is immune to misinformation. Today you've brought a story about your own research.
  2. Dr Amelia Hart:I have, and it's slightly embarrassing. Two years ago my team ran a small study. Sixty students took a ten-minute walk before a memory test, and sixty didn't. The walkers scored, on average, about four per cent higher.
  3. Host:That sounds like good news.
  4. Dr Amelia Hart:It was a modest, interesting result. But the difference was small, the sample was tiny, and all the volunteers were students from one university. In the paper we wrote that a short walk may be associated with slightly better recall, and we listed every caveat.
  5. Host:So what went wrong?
  6. Dr Amelia Hart:First the university's press office got involved. Their press release said that walking appears to boost memory. Still fairly cautious. But then a newspaper picked it up, and the headline read: Scientists prove a daily walk makes you cleverer.
  7. Host:Prove!
  8. Dr Amelia Hart:Exactly. Nobody had proved anything. We'd found a correlation in one group of young people, not a causal link. Within a week, a wellness website was claiming that walking can raise your IQ by thirty per cent. Where that number came from, I still have no idea.
  9. Host:Did you try to correct it?
  10. Dr Amelia Hart:I wrote to the newspaper, and they added a line at the bottom of the article. But by then the story had been shared hundreds of thousands of times. Corrections are generally thought to reach only a fraction of the people who saw the original.
  11. Host:So what should listeners do when they see a headline like that?
  12. Dr Amelia Hart:Ask three questions. How many people were studied? Who were they? And does the study actually say what the headline says? If it sounds too good to be true, take it with a pinch of salt.

According to Dr Hart, the main problem was that…

Where did the «thirty per cent» figure come from?

c Who said it — the paper, the press release, the headline or the website? Notice how the claim gets stronger at every step. The words that kept it cautious (may be associated with, appears to) are the grammar of the next stage.

  1. A short walk may be associated with slightly better recall. →
  2. Walking appears to boost memory. →

distancing: it is said that · is thought to have

12 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. When you report a claim you cannot check yourself — like the «thirty per cent» — you distance yourself from it. The examples follow Dr Hart's story.

Grammar Bank1Bdistancing — passive reporting structures
structureexamplenote
It + passive + thatIt is claimed that walking boosts memory.say, think, believe, claim, report, estimate, know, consider
subject + passive + to + verbWalking is said to boost memory.the claim is about now / in general
subject + passive + to be + -ingThe website is reported to be changing its headline.happening at the moment
subject + passive + to have + V3The figure is thought to have come from a blog.happened earlier
subject + passive + to have been + V3The story is estimated to have been shared 300,000 times.earlier + passive
There + passive + to be / to have beenThere are said to be dozens of similar stories.«there is» → there is said to be
  • The reporting verb can be in the past: It was thought that… / He was thought to have left.
  • This is typical of news and academic writing: it shows that you are not responsible for the claim.
  • ✗ It is said the study to be flawed. → ✓ It is said that the study is flawed. / ✓ The study is said to be flawed.

Подсказка. «Говорят / считается, что…» → It is said / thought that… или X is said / thought to…. Если действие было раньше момента, о котором говорят, — to have + V3: «Считается, что цифру придумал блогер» → The figure is thought to have been invented by a blogger.

  1. The headline to have been shared over three hundred thousand times.

  4. Dr Hart is said on a follow-up study at the moment.
  5. There to be dozens of similar stories online.
  6. The original paper to be quite cautious.

Lost in translation

12 min

a Dr Hart's story is not unusual. Read the feature article about science hype. Then answer the questions.

Lost in translation: how a modest finding becomes a miracleA feature article · about 380 words

A Science, it would seem, has never been more popular. Health stories tend to be among the most widely read items on any news website, and a single eye-catching study can travel around the world in an afternoon. Yet researchers increasingly complain that what reaches the public bears little resemblance to what they actually found.

B The problem does not appear to start in newsrooms. One frequently cited analysis of university press releases found that a sizeable proportion of them contained exaggerations — advice the original papers never gave, or claims of cause and effect based on purely correlational data. More strikingly, when a press release exaggerated, the news stories based on it were considerably more likely to exaggerate too. Journalists, it seems, largely reproduce the spin they are handed.

C Why would scientists' own institutions overstate their work? Part of the answer is presumably competition: universities compete for funding, students and attention, and a cautious headline rarely goes viral. Researchers, too, may be tempted to go along with the hype; a study that makes the news is arguably more likely to attract future grants. Caveats, meanwhile, tend to be buried in the final paragraph — if they survive at all.

D Readers are not entirely blameless either. We seem to prefer clear, confident answers to messy, provisional ones, and a story that confirms what we already suspect — that chocolate is secretly good for us, say — is shared far more readily than one that contradicts it. To some extent, then, the hype is a response to demand.

E There are, apparently, some grounds for optimism. Research suggests that adding caveats to press releases does not appear to reduce media coverage, which would seem to undermine the main argument for exaggeration. If that finding holds, the solution may be surprisingly simple: say what the evidence shows, and no more.

1. In paragraph A, the writer suggests that…

2. According to paragraph B, exaggeration in the news…

3. The writer mentions chocolate in paragraph D to illustrate…

4. In paragraph E, the writer's attitude is…

  3. temporary and likely to change (paragraph D) →
  4. free from responsibility for something bad (paragraph D) →
  5. weaken (an argument) (paragraph E) →

  3. Part of the answer is presumably competition. →
  4. Researchers, too, may be tempted to go along with the hype. →
  5. A study that makes the news is arguably more likely to attract future grants. →

hedging: seem · appear · tend · may well

10 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. The examples are from the article. Hedging makes a claim exactly as strong as the evidence — no stronger.

Grammar Bank1Bhedging
toolexamplenote
seem / appear + to (be / be -ing / have + V3)The effect seems to be small. The figure appears to have been invented.negative: does not appear to
it seems / appears / would seem that · there seems / appears to beIt would seem that the hype is a response to demand. There appears to be a link.would = even more tentative
tend toCaveats tend to be buried at the end.= usually, in general
may / might / could (well)Researchers may be tempted. It could well have been a coincidence.well = quite likely
adverbsapparently (I've heard) · allegedly (claimed, not proved) · reportedly · supposedly (I doubt it) · presumably (I assume) · arguably (one could argue)usually before the main verb or at the start
softenersto some extent, in some cases, a sizeable proportion of, relativelyavoid «all», «always», «prove»
  • Don't over-hedge: ✗ It might possibly perhaps seem that… One hedge per claim is usually enough.
  • ✗ The effect seems that it is small. → ✓ The effect seems to be small. / ✓ It seems that the effect is small.

Подсказка. По-русски это «по-видимому», «как правило», «судя по всему», «якобы», «пожалуй». allegedly = «якобы» (об обвинениях), apparently = «судя по всему / говорят», presumably = «надо полагать», arguably = «пожалуй, можно утверждать». В эссе C1 такие слова — признак зрелого стиля.

  1. The manager knew about the problem — that is what the newspaper claims, but nothing has been proved.
  2. It's the most important health study of the decade — though not everyone would agree.
  3. She isn't answering her phone. She's still in the lab — she usually works late on Fridays.
  4. , the journalist never read the original paper — at least, that's what her colleague told me.
  5. The effect to be smaller in older adults.
  6. There to be a link between sleep and memory.

  2. Lily:Hi, Sam! Yes. Gran is eighty next Saturday, and we're throwing her a surprise party!

Grammar Bank2Athe future: present continuous and be going to
formwhen?example

Zoe's blog

9 min

a Now read Zoe's blog about her first shift. Find six words from the Vocabulary Bank. Was the day a disaster?

Zoe's blog · «My first shift»

Last summer I got my first job: I was a waitress at The Blue Wave, a little café by the beach. I had never worked before, so I was excited — and very nervous.

On the morning of my first shift, I opened my eyes, looked at the clock and realised it was ten past nine. My shift started at nine! I had overslept. My phone had run out of battery in the night, so my alarm hadn't gone off. I put on my uniform and rushed to the café without breakfast.

When I arrived, the café was already full of customers, and the manager, Rosa, was waiting for me at the door. She didn't look happy. «Table six,» she said. «Three hot chocolates. Quickly!»

I was carrying the hot chocolates to table six when I tripped over a bag. I spilt one all over a customer's white shirt! I apologised again and again. I was so embarrassed that my face went redder than the tomatoes in the kitchen.

But then something strange happened: the customer started laughing. It turned out that his daughter had filmed everything on her phone. That evening she posted the video online with the title «The Hot Chocolate Girl», and by the next morning it had gone viral.

When I came to work the next day, there was a long queue outside the café. Everyone wanted to meet the hot chocolate girl! I was panicking, but Rosa smiled and told me to calm down. In the end, my terrible first day turned out to be the best advert the café had ever had.

The blog post is about…

narrative tenses

a Read the Grammar Bank. Every example is from Zoe's story. A good story needs three past tenses.Все примеры — из истории Зои.

Grammar Bank2Anarrative tenses: past simple · past continuous · past perfect
formuseexample
past simpleV2 / -edthe main events, one after anotherI put on my uniform and rushed to the café.
past continuouswas / were + -ingthe background; an action in progress when something happenedI was carrying the hot chocolates when I tripped.
past perfecthad + V3an earlier action: it happened before another past actionI realised I had overslept. My phone had run out of battery.
  • 'd = had: I'd overslept. Negative: hadn't + V3: My alarm hadn't gone off.
  • Use the past perfect only when you go back in time. Events in order → past simple: I woke up, got dressed and left.
  • V3 to remember: oversleep → overslept, run → run, go → gone, spill → spilt / spilled, see → seen.

Подсказка. В русском одно прошедшее время, а в английском рассказе видно, что случилось раньше: «Я поняла, что проспала» = I realised that I had overslept. Past continuous — фон («несла чашки»), past simple — события («споткнулась»), past perfect — шаг назад.

a Zoe's story was in the news. Listen to «Work Talk» — the radio show from our last lesson. Rosa and Zoe tell the full story. Why was Rosa so stressed that morning?Радиошоу «Work Talk» из прошлого урока: Роза и Зоя рассказывают всю историю.

Radio: «Work Talk»Listen first · Use 🐢 if it's fast · Text at the end
  1. Host:Welcome back to «Work Talk». Last week we met people with unusual jobs. Today: first days at work. With me are Rosa, who runs a café by the beach, and Zoe, her youngest waitress. Rosa, what happened on Zoe's first day?
  2. Rosa, café manager:Well, it was a crazy morning. We had opened at eight, and by nine the café was already full. Two waiters had called in sick, so I was doing three jobs at once. And my new waitress wasn't there!
  3. Host:Zoe, what had happened?
  4. Zoe:I'd overslept! My phone had died in the night, so my alarm didn't go off. I woke up at ten past nine.
  5. Host:Had you ever worked in a café before?
  6. Zoe:No, never. I'd only done some babysitting. I'd watched lots of videos about how to carry three cups at once, but it's not the same in real life!

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаam / is / are + -ing
1
Одна мысль

Когда что-то происходит сейчас или в эти дни (now, today, this week), говорим: am / is / are + глагол-ing. «Дэниел стоит у школы (прямо сейчас)» → Daniel is standing. «Не» — not: I'm not teaching. В вопросе am / is / are идёт вперёд: Are you teaching?

2
Формула-конструктор
I+'m+standing+in front of the school.
They+'re+having+a break.

I → am (I'm) · he / she / it → is (he's, it's) · we / you / they → are (we're, they're)
-ing: teach → teaching · have → having (без e) · swim → swimming, sit → sitting

He+isn't+teaching+this week.
Are+you+having+a good time?

Короткий ответ: Yes, I am. / No, I'm not. · Yes, they are. / No, they aren't. · Yes, it is. (не «Yes, it's»)

нужно -ing

a Daniel writes a blog for his school website. Read it. What is it about?Дэниел пишет блог для сайта своей школы. Прочитайте: о чём он?

Our week in St Petersburg

Hello from St Petersburg! This week ten of our pupils and I are visiting our partner school, and we're having a wonderful time.

At home in Manchester, I get up at half past six and go to school by bike. I teach five lessons a day, and I check homework every evening. But this week is different! I'm not teaching, and I'm not checking homework. I'm staying in a small hotel, and I'm walking to school — no bike!

Our pupils are staying with Russian host families. They're practising their Russian all day, and they're learning a lot. At this school, lessons start at half past eight, and the pupils stand up when a teacher comes in. Our pupils love it!

Right now I'm sitting in the staff room and writing this blog. My Russian colleagues are drinking tea and talking about the timetable. It's raining again, but we don't mind!

See you next week! — Mr Jones

What the Coach Said

After losing his biggest client, Tom works with a productivity coach. Habits and productivity phrases, and reported speech: She said… She told me to… She asked me if…

“We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.”Will Durant

  8. Tom:Everything? Even social media?

  10. Tom:OK. What else?

  14. Tom:Great. I'm going to start tomorrow.
  15. Maya (coach):Tomorrow? Why not today?
  16. Tom:Ha! Fair point. I'm starting today.

reported statements

15 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. The examples are from Tom's coaching session. When we report, the verb usually goes one step back into the past.

Grammar Bank2Breported statements
direct speechreported speechchange
«I get distracted.»He said (that) he got distracted.present simple → past simple
«I'm starting today.»He said he was starting that day.present continuous → past continuous
«I lost my biggest client.»He said he had lost his biggest client.past simple → past perfect
«I've never kept track of my time.»He said he had never kept track of his time.present perfect → past perfect
«I'll call you.»She said she would call him.will → would
«I can't stay focused.»He said he couldn't stay focused.can → could
«I'm going to start tomorrow.»He said he was going to start the next day.am going to → was going to
  • say something (to someone): She said (that)… · tell someone something: She told me (that)… — ✗ She said me.
  • Pronouns and time words change too: today → that day · tomorrow → the next day · next Friday → the following Friday · here → there.
  • If something is still true now, the verb can stay the same: She said big tasks scare us. In the exercises below, move the verb back.
  • that is optional: She told me (that) I was on track.

Подсказка. По-русски «Она сказала, что я молодец» — время не меняется. По-английски после said / told глагол обычно «сдвигается назад»: present → past, past → past perfect, will → would, can → could.

Tom's blog: week one

9 min

a A week later Maya calls Tom, as she promised. Tom writes about the call on his blog — in reported speech. Read. Is Tom on track?

Tom's blog · «Week one with a coach»

On Friday Maya called me, as she had promised. First she asked me if I had kept track of my time. I said I had, and I showed her my notes. The shock of the week: I had spent eleven hours on social media!

Maya didn't get angry. She asked me how I felt about it. I told her I was a bit embarrassed. Then she asked me where my phone had been while I was working. I admitted it had been on my desk, right next to my laptop.

So she gave me new instructions. She told me to put my phone in the kitchen, and she asked me to send her a photo of my desk every morning — with no phone on it! She also told me not to work for more than fifty minutes without a break.

At the end, I asked her when I would see results. She said it usually took about two months to form a new habit, but that I was already on track. Not bad for week one!

Is Tom on track after week one?

reported questions and instructions

13 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. The examples are from Tom's blog.

Grammar Bank2Breported questions and instructions
direct speechreported speech
yes / no question«Did you keep track of your time?»She asked me if (whether) I had kept track of my time.
wh- question«How do you feel about it?»
«When will I see results?»		She asked me how I felt about it.
I asked her when I would see results.
instruction«Put your phone in the kitchen.»
«Don't work for more than fifty minutes.»		She told me to put my phone in the kitchen.
She told me not to work for more than fifty minutes.
request«Can you send me a photo?» · «Please send me a photo.»She asked me to send her a photo.
  • A reported question is not a question any more: no do / did, statement word order, no question mark. ✗ She asked me how did I feel. ✓ She asked me how I felt.
  • Yes / no questions: if or whether.
  • Instructions: told + person + (not) to + verb. Requests: asked + person + to + verb. ✗ She told me don't work.

Подсказка. Косвенный вопрос — уже не вопрос: прямой порядок слов (подлежащее + глагол), без do / did. Русское «ли» = if / whether. Просьбы и указания: asked / told + кого + (not) to + глагол.

  1. «Did you enjoy the session?» → Anna asked Tom the session.
  2. «Where do you work?» → Maya asked Tom .
  3. «Can you send me a photo?» → She asked me her a photo.
  4. «Don't check your phone!» → She told me my phone.
  5. «Will it really work?» → Tom asked really work.
  6. «Why did you get a coach?» → She asked me why a coach.

b Report the questions. Remember: no do / did, and statement word order.Передайте вопросы: без do / did, прямой порядок слов.

  1. «Are you busy?» → She asked me busy.
  2. «Where do you live?» → He asked me where .
  3. «Have you set a goal?» → Maya asked Tom a goal.
  4. «What time does the meeting start?» → I asked what time .
  5. «Did you stick to the plan?» → She asked me to the plan.
  6. «How long will it take?» → He asked how long .

c Report the instructions and requests with told / asked + (not) to.told / asked + кого + (not) to + глагол.

  1. Maya to Tom: «Write down everything you do.» → Maya told Tom down everything he did.
  2. Maya to Tom: «Don't try to change everything at once.» → She told him to change everything at once.
  3. Tom to Anna: «Please hide my phone!» → Tom asked Anna his phone.
  4. Anna to Tom: «Don't work after ten.» → Anna told Tom after ten.
  5. The boss to the team: «Prioritise the urgent tasks.» → The boss told the team the urgent tasks.

There's… It's… — Grammar Easy

12 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat. All the examples are from Anna's town.Прочитайте четыре шага. Нажмите 🔊 и повторите. Все примеры — из города Анны.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаThere's… It's…
1
Одна мысль

Сначала говорим, что ЕСТЬ (новое место): There's (There is) + a café. Потом говорим о нём — где оно, какое оно: уже It's (It is). Много вещей: There are two cafés → They're in the square. Вопрос «где?»: Where's the café? — It's next to the bank.

2
Формула-конструктор
There's+a café+in Market Street.
It's+next to+the bank.

Новое → There's a… · Уже знаем → It's… · Много → There are… → They're…

There are+two cafés+in the square.
They're+next to+the museum.
Where's+the café?+— It's+next to the bank.
3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • There's a café in Market Street. It's next to the bank.
  • There's a pharmacy. It's opposite the bus stop.
  • There are three museums. They're in the centre.
  • Where's the bus stop? — It's next to the museum.
4
Осторожно!
❌ There's a café. There's next to the bank. → ✅ There's a café. It's next to the bank.
Второй раз — уже It's.
❌ Where's the café? — Is next to the bank. → ✅ It's next to the bank.
Не забывайте It!
❌ Where is the shops? → ✅ Where are the shops?
Много → Where are…? — They're…

some / any — Grammar Easy

9 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat. The examples are from the walk with Anna.Прочитайте четыре шага, слушайте и повторяйте. Примеры — из прогулки с Анной.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаsome / any
1
Одна мысль

Когда вещей много (shops, cafés), в обычном предложении (+) говорим some — «несколько, какие-то». В предложении с not (−) и в вопросе (?) — any. Одна вещь — как раньше, a: There isn't a cinema. Is there a market?

2
Формула-конструктор
There are+some+shops.
There aren't+any+cinemas.
Are there+any+restaurants?

+ → some · − и ? → any · Ответ: Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.

3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • There are some nice shops in Bridge Street.
  • There aren't any cinemas.
  • Are there any good restaurants? — Yes, there are.
  • There are some lovely cakes at the market.
4
Осторожно!
❌ There are any shops. → ✅ There are some shops.
+ → some.
❌ There aren't some cinemas. → ✅ There aren't any cinemas.
− → any.
❌ Is there any cafés? → ✅ Are there any cafés?
Много → Are there…?

«Travel Talk» · Five questions for Kate, 26

Kate writes a travel blog. You may remember her story about a trip to Rome. This week she answered our questions.

How many countries have you been to?
Fourteen! I went abroad for the first time when I was nineteen — to Spain. I loved it, and I've travelled every year since then.

Have you ever been backpacking?
Yes, I have. Two years ago I went backpacking in Asia for three months. I stayed in hostels and met lots of amazing people.

Have you ever missed a flight?
Yes, twice! The first time was in Paris. I was buying souvenirs at the airport and I didn't hear the announcement. My plane took off without me!

What's the strangest food you've ever tried?
Fried insects in Thailand. A local gave them to me at a night market. They were crunchy — and not bad, actually!

Is there anything you've never done?
Lots of things! I've never been on a guided tour — I prefer to explore on my own and get lost. And I've never been to Portugal. But that's going to change: I'm flying to Lisbon tomorrow!

Kate is…

present perfect: experiences

a Read the Grammar Bank. The examples are from Kate's interview.Примеры — из интервью Кейт.

Grammar Bank2Apresent perfect: ever / never → past simple for details
formexample
+I / you / we / they have ('ve) + V3 · he / she has ('s) + V3I've been to fourteen countries. She's tried fried insects.
–haven't / hasn't + V3 · 've never + V3I've never been to Portugal.
?Have / Has + person + ever + V3?Have you ever missed a flight? — Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.
  • Experience (when? — not important) → present perfect. Details (when? where? what happened?) → past simple: Have you ever missed a flight? — Yes, I have. I missed a flight in Paris two years ago.
  • With yesterday, last year, in 2019, two years ago, when I was… → only past simple. ✗ I've been to Spain in 2019. ✓ I went to Spain in 2019.
  • been to = went and came back: She's been to Paris. · gone to = she is there now: She's gone to Lisbon.
  • V3: be → been, see → seen, eat → eaten, fly → flown, take → taken, meet → met, lose → lost, try → tried.

Подсказка. «Ты когда-нибудь…?» = Have you ever…? Опыт «вообще в жизни» — present perfect. Как только появляется «когда?» (ago, last, in 2019) — past simple.

Radio phone-in: «What Would You Do?»Listen first · Use 🐢 if it's fast · Text at the end
  1. Kate (host):Good evening and welcome to «What Would You Do?», the show where you call us with a problem and our listeners help you sort it out. Our first caller is Ben. Hi, Ben!
  2. Ben:Hi, Kate. Well, last week I bought an old sofa online. It was really cheap — only forty pounds. When I got it home, I found an envelope inside it. There was two thousand pounds in it!
  3. Kate (host):Wow! And what did you do?
  4. Ben:Nothing yet. I can't figure out what to do. Part of me says, «Keep it — nobody will find out.» But I feel guilty.
  5. Kate (host):Well, if I were you, I'd give it back. It isn't your money.
  6. Ben:I know, but the seller lives in a huge house. If I gave the money back, she probably wouldn't even notice!
  7. Kate (host):Let's hear from a listener. Lisa, you're on the air.
  8. Lisa:Hi, Ben. Something similar happened to me once. I found a wallet on a train and I handed it in at the station. A week later the owner found me and gave me a reward! And honestly, if you kept the money, you would feel terrible every time you sat on that sofa.
  9. Ben:Ha! That's true. But what if she asked me why I didn't call her earlier? I'd have to make up an excuse.
  10. Lisa:You don't need an excuse. Just tell her the truth. If I were in your shoes, I'd call her today.
  11. Kate (host):So, Ben, what are you going to do?
  12. Ben:OK, you're right. I'll do the right thing. If I find her phone number, I'll call her tomorrow. And if she doesn't answer, I'll go to her house.
  13. Kate (host):Great! Call us next week and tell us what happened.

second conditional

13 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. All the examples are like Kate's and Lisa's advice. Look at the two colours: if + past, then would + verb.Прочитайте Grammar Bank. Две части: if + прошедшая форма, would + глагол.

Grammar Bank2Asecond conditional — imagined situations
IF + past formIf I found money,found · were · had · kept · could
,
would ('d) / wouldn't + verbI would give it back.I'd call · she'd feel · we wouldn't keep

Past form, but not past time! It is about now or the future — but it is imagined, not real.

❌ If I would find money, I would give it back.
❌ If I found money, I'll give it back.
❌ If I am you, I'll call her.
✅ If I found money, I would give it back. (no would after if!)
✅ If I found money, I'd give it back.
✅ If I were you, I'd call her. (advice)
  • Advice: If I were you, I'd… = «на твоём месте я бы…». If I was you is common in conversation, but were is better.
  • The if-part can come second — then no comma: I'd give it back if I found it.
  • Questions: What would you do if you found £2,000?

Подсказка. По-русски «бы» стоит в обеих частях: «Если бы я нашёл деньги, я бы их вернул». В английском would («бы») — только в одной части, а после if — прошедшая форма: If I found…, I would…

From: Ben · To: «What Would You Do?»an email · about 170 words

Hi Kate, it's Ben — the man with the sofa! I want to tell you what happened. I found out the seller's name, Mrs Grant, from the website, and I called her. At first she didn't believe me! Then she started crying. The money was her husband's. He died two years ago, and she didn't know that he had hidden money in the sofa.

She was so happy that she gave me two hundred pounds as a thank-you present. I'm really glad I did the right thing. To be honest, if I found money again, I'd give it back straight away.

1st · real, possibleIf I find it, I'll give it back.If + present, will ('ll) + verb

irregular verbs — Grammar Easy

12 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat. All the examples are from Ben's day.Прочитайте четыре шага, слушайте и повторяйте. Все примеры — из дня Бена.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаPast Simple: irregular verbs
1
Одна мысль

Многие частые глаголы в прошедшем времени не берут -ed — они меняются: go → went, buy → bought. Их учим, как слова (карточки!). Хорошая новость: «нет» и вопрос — как в прошлый раз: didn't / Did + глагол в обычной форме: I didn't go. Did you go?

2
Формула-конструктор
I+went+to Brighton.
I+didn't+go+to London.
Did+you+go+to the sea?+— Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.

go → went · get → got · have → had · see → saw · take → took · eat → ate · buy → bought · meet → met · swim → swam · come → came · sit → sat · lose → lost · find → found

3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • We went to Brighton by train.
  • We had fish and chips on the beach.
  • Joe ate an ice cream.
  • Joe didn't swim.
  • Did you buy anything?
4
Осторожно!
❌ I goed to the sea. → ✅ I went to the sea.
go → went: учим, как слово.
❌ I didn't went. → ✅ I didn't go.
После didn't — обычная форма.
❌ Did you saw the sea? → ✅ Did you see the sea?
После Did — обычная форма.

Where did you go? — Grammar Easy

10 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat the questions.Прочитайте четыре шага. Повторите вопросы.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаWhere did you go?
1
Одна мысль

Вопрос о прошлом с вопросительным словом — как конструктор: вопросительное слово + did + you / he / she… + глагол в обычной форме. Did — маленький помощник прошлого, поэтому глагол уже без -ed и без went: Where did you go? What did you buy?

2
Формула-конструктор
Where+did+you+go?
What+did+Joe+eat?
When+did+they+come home?

Where? — где, куда · When? — когда · What? — что · Who? — кто, кого · What time? — во сколько · How? — как

3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • Where did you go? — To Brighton.
  • How did you get there? — By train.
  • What time did you come home? — At ten.
  • Who did you meet? — An old friend.
4
Осторожно!
❌ Where you went? → ✅ Where did you go?
Нужен помощник did.
❌ What did you bought? → ✅ What did you buy?
После did — обычная форма.
❌ When did come you home? → ✅ When did you come home?
Порядок: did + you + глагол.

  4. did you come home? — On Sunday evening.
  5. did you buy? — A T-shirt.
  6. did you go with? — With my brother.

c Step 2. Choose the right question.Шаг 2. Выберите правильный вопрос.

d Step 3. Write the question.Шаг 3. Напишите вопрос.

  5. (Joe / swim) in the sea?

A New Chapter

Two years after moving to Edinburgh, Anna has set up a bakery. Starting again, a podcast and a blog — and the bridge from the past to now: for, since, ago, present perfect simple and continuous.

“Rome wasn't built in a day.”English proverb
B1Starting againPresent perfectfor · since · ago60–70 min

Anna's new chapter

a Listen to the podcast «New Chapters». Anna is the guest. What is the conversation mainly about?

Podcast: «New Chapters»Listen first · Use 🐢 if it's fast · Text at the end
  1. James (host):Welcome to «New Chapters», the podcast about people who start again. My guest today is Anna. She moved from Kazan to Edinburgh two years ago, and now she runs a small Russian bakery. Anna, welcome!
  2. Anna:Thanks, James! Sorry if I sound tired — I've been baking since five o'clock this morning.
  3. James (host):Five o'clock! So, what did you use to do in Kazan?
  4. Anna:I used to work in a bank. It was a good job, but I wasn't happy. When I moved here, I felt really homesick, and I missed my mum's pies. So I started baking them at home.
  5. James (host):And people liked them?
  6. Anna:They loved them! Then my neighbour asked me to make fifty pies for her wedding. That was the moment I decided to take a risk. I set up the bakery from scratch and opened it in April.
  7. James (host):So you've had the bakery for six months now. How's it going?
  8. Anna:Better than I expected! We don't advertise — it's all word of mouth. Some of our regulars have been coming every day since we opened.
  9. James (host):What's been the hardest thing?
  10. Anna:The early mornings! I still haven't got used to getting up at four. But all the hard work has paid off.
  11. James (host):And have you settled in? Have you made friends?
  12. Anna:Yes, I have. I've been taking Scottish dancing classes since January — that's where I've made most of my friends. And I keep in touch with my family every day. My mum has visited twice. She's tried every pie!
  13. James (host):I'm sure she approved! Anna, thank you so much.

The conversation is mainly about…

for · since · ago

14 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. All the examples are from Anna's story.Все примеры — из истории Анны.

Grammar Bank1Bpast simple or present perfect? for · since · ago
timeformexampletime words
finished — a time in the pastpast simpleShe moved to Edinburgh two years ago. When did she open the bakery? — In April.ago, in April, last year, yesterday, when I was…
from the past until nowpresent perfect (simple or continuous)She's lived in Edinburgh for two years. She's had the bakery since April. How long have you been learning English?for, since, How long…?, all my life
  • for + a period: for six months, for ages · since + a starting point: since April, since 2024, since I moved here · ago + a period, with the past simple: two years ago.
  • How long…? → present perfect. When…? → past simple.
  • State verbs (know, have = own, be, like) — present perfect simple only: I've known her for years. ✗ I've been knowing

Подсказка. По-русски «Я живу здесь два года» — настоящее время, а по-английски — present perfect: I've lived / I've been living here for two years. ✗ I live here for two years. ✗ I'm living here since 2024.

  1. Anna to Edinburgh two years ago.
  2. She in Edinburgh for two years, and she loves it.
  3. She the bakery since April.
  4. the bakery? — In April.
  5. How long Scottish dancing? — Since January.
  6. I my best friend for twenty years.

b for, since or ago?for, since или ago?

  1. She has had the bakery six months.
  2. She has been dancing January.
  3. She moved to Scotland two years .

A Saturday at Babushka's Kitchen

9 min

a Anna calls her bakery «Babushka's Kitchen». Read her blog post from last Saturday. How does she feel at the end of the day?

Babushka's Kitchen · Saturday, 3 p.m.

It's three o'clock and I've been on my feet since five this morning. We've sold over three hundred pies today, and we've completely run out of cabbage pies. Sorry, everyone!

My hands are covered in flour because I've been making dough all afternoon. Ivan, my new assistant, has only been working here for two weeks, but he's already learned all my mum's recipes. He's a star.

I've been trying to make the perfect honey cake all week. I've baked it five times, and I think I've finally got it right — the regulars have tried it, and they love it!

Two years ago I didn't know anyone in this city. Today a customer said, «Your bakery feels like home.» I've never been so happy.

1. How many pies has the bakery sold today?

2. Why are Anna's hands covered in flour?

3. How long has Ivan been working at the bakery?

4. How many times has Anna baked the honey cake?

b Look at the verbs. Is the sentence about the result (what is done, how many?) or about the activity (what she has been doing, how long?)? This is the grammar of the next stage.Результат (сколько? что сделано?) или процесс (чем занималась, как долго?) — это грамматика следующего этапа.

  1. We've sold over three hundred pies today. →
  2. I've been making dough all afternoon. →
  3. He's already learned all my mum's recipes. →
  4. I've been trying to make the perfect honey cake all week. →
  5. I've baked it five times. →
  6. He's only been working here for two weeks. →

present perfect simple or continuous?

12 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. The examples are from Anna's blog.Примеры — из блога Анны.

Grammar Bank1Bpresent perfect simple vs continuous
present perfect simple
have / has + V3		present perfect continuous
have / has been + -ing
focusthe result: what is done, how many, how many timesthe activity: how long; often not finished, or it explains what we can see now
examplesWe've sold 300 pies. He's learned all the recipes. I've baked it five times.I've been baking since five. My hands are covered in flour — I've been making dough.
questionsHow many pies have you sold?How long have you been waiting?
  • State verbs (know, have = own, be, like, love, understand) — simple only: I've known Ivan for years.
  • live, work, study, teach + for / since — both forms are fine: I've lived / I've been living here for two years.

Подсказка. «Сколько сделал? Что готово?» → simple. «Чем занимался и как долго (и, может быть, ещё занимаюсь)?» → continuous.

  1. I'm exhausted. I since five o'clock.

  5. How many times the honey cake?
  6. Your eyes are red. ?

Seeing Isn't Believing

A video call where every face was fake: deepfakes, scams and misinformation. Grammar: the passive in all its forms and the reporting passive — It is said that… · is believed to…

“Seeing is believing.”English proverb — but is it still true?

the call that never happened

12 min

a Now read a news article about a real-looking call that never happened. Find six words from the Vocabulary Bank. Then answer: what is the article mainly about?

«The call that never happened»

Last month, a finance manager at a mid-sized logistics company in Manchester was tricked into sending two million pounds to criminals. The money has not been recovered, and the case is still being investigated by the police.

It all began with an email. The manager, who has not been named, was asked to join an urgent video call about a «confidential deal». On the call he could see the company's finance director and three other colleagues. Their faces were familiar and their voices were convincing — but every one of them was fake. The faces and voices had been generated by AI from videos that had been posted online after conferences and company events.

«I was taken in completely,» he told investigators. «They looked and sounded exactly like my colleagues.» During the call he was told to make fifteen payments to five different bank accounts. The scam was only discovered a week later, when he mentioned the deal to the real finance director.

Experts say the case shows how fast the technology is improving. Only a few years ago, deepfakes could be detected quite easily: the faces didn't blink, and the voices sounded robotic. Today a convincing fake can be made in a few hours with free software.

So what can be done? According to security specialists, large payments should always be verified through a second channel, such as a phone call to a known number. «If a request feels urgent and secret, that's the giveaway,» says one adviser. The company has since introduced new rules: from next month, no payment over ten thousand pounds will be made without a face-to-face check.

The article is mainly about…

4. According to the article, deepfakes today…

5. What is «the giveaway», according to the adviser?

c The article is full of the passive (be + past participle): we don't know or don't care who did it. Which form is each phrase? This is the grammar of the next stage.

  1. the case is still being investigated →
  2. The money has not been recovered →
  3. The faces and voices had been generated by AI →
  4. he was told to make fifteen payments →
  5. no payment will be made →
  6. large payments should always be verified →

the passive: all forms

15 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. All the passive examples come from the article.

Grammar Bank2Athe passive — all forms
formactivepassive: be + V3
present simpleBanks check large payments.Large payments are checked.
present continuousThe police are investigating the case.The case is being investigated.
past simpleSomeone told him to pay.He was told to pay.
present perfectNobody has recovered the money.The money has not been recovered.
past perfectAI had generated the faces.The faces had been generated by AI.
futureThe company will make no payment…No payment will be made…
modalYou should verify payments.Payments should be verified.
infinitive / -ing—Nobody wants to be fooled. I hate being asked for passwords.
  • We use the passive when the doer is unknown, unimportant or obvious, and in news and reports. Add by + doer only if it is important: generated by AI.
  • Only the form of be changes; the main verb is always V3: is checked · was checked · has been checked · will be checked.
  • Informal English often uses get: He got fooled.

Подсказка. В русском часто «-ся» или «неопределённо-личная» форма: «Дело расследуется» = The case is being investigated; «Ему сказали» = He was told.

  1. The case by the police at the moment.
  2. The fake faces from conference videos.
  3. Since 2020, millions of deepfakes online.
  4. In future, every large payment twice.
  5. A convincing fake voice can in minutes.
  6. Nobody likes by a machine.

Byte Size: the expert view

10 min

a The story reached the tech podcast «Byte Size». Listen to Nina and Owen, an expert on online fraud. What is Owen's main message?

Podcast: «Byte Size»Listen first · Use 🐢 if it's fast · Text at the end
  1. Nina (host):Welcome to «Byte Size». Last month's deepfake video call is still all over the news. Owen, you study online fraud. How common are these scams?
  2. Owen:More common than people think. It's estimated that deepfake fraud has grown ten times in the last two years. And most cases are never reported, because companies are embarrassed.
  3. Nina (host):Who's behind them?
  4. Owen:Organised groups, mostly. The scammers in the Manchester case are believed to be based abroad, and they're thought to have used free software. Nothing cutting-edge, really.
  5. Nina (host):That's scary. And the manager is said to have been very experienced.
  6. Owen:Exactly, and that's the point. People say, «I would never be taken in.» But these fakes imitate faces, voices, even the way people move. It's not about being stupid. It's about trust.
  7. Nina (host):So how can we detect a deepfake?
  8. Owen:There used to be giveaways, like strange blinking or bad lip-sync. Those are disappearing. It's now thought that the best protection isn't a piece of technology, it's a process. If someone asks for money, hang up and call them back on a number you know.
  9. Nina (host):And will AI tools help?
  10. Owen:Some detection tools are said to be ninety per cent accurate. But don't rely on them completely. The criminals are using AI too.
  11. Nina (host):Owen, thank you. And listeners: if your boss asks for money on a video call, call them back first!

Owen's main message is that…

reporting passive

12 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. The examples are from the podcast. This is the language of news reports — and very useful in B2 First essays and reports.

Grammar Bank2Ait is said that… · is believed to… · is thought to have…
patternexample
It + is said / believed / thought / reported / estimated / known + that + clauseIt's estimated that deepfake fraud has grown ten times.
person / thing + is said / believed / thought + to + infinitive (now)The scammers are believed to be based abroad.
person / thing + is said / believed / thought + to have + V3 (before now)They are thought to have used free software. The manager is said to have been very experienced.
  • Verbs: say, believe, think, report, know, expect, estimate, consider, claim.
  • Not ✗ The scammers are believed that they are abroad. → It is believed that the scammers are… / The scammers are believed to be…
  • Past reporting: It was thought that… · He was believed to be…

Подсказка. «Говорят, что…», «Считается, что…», «Полагают, что…» — информация без источника. Сейчас → to + глагол; раньше → to have + V3.

  1. It that most online content will soon be AI-generated.
  2. The scammers are believed in another country.
  3. The fake video is thought by a teenager last year.
  4. It is known deepfakes are used in scams.
  5. The new tool is said ninety per cent of fakes.
  6. The manager to have followed all the rules.

  1. It is said that the app collects too much data. → The app too much data.
  2. It is believed that the hackers are students. → The hackers students.
  3. It is thought that the scammers used free software. → The scammers free software.
  4. It is reported that the company lost two million pounds. → The company two million pounds.
  5. People say that the new chatbot is very convincing. → The new chatbot very convincing.
  6. It is known that the director's voice was copied. → The director's voice copied.

  1. The criminals are believed abroad now.
  2. The criminals are believed the money last month.
  3. Deepfake tools are expected even cheaper next year.
  4. The video is said ten million times before it was deleted.
